Emphasis of Matter: Note No 40 – In reference to Note 29(F) of the standalone financial statements of the associate, regarding the reassessment of the tax liability consequent to the Income Tax Department's proposal to substitute the regulatory price adopted by the associate company for captive consumption of bagasse with market price data, thereby nullifying the Section 80-IA deduction claimed by the associate company. The associate company has reversed MAT credit entitlement of Rs 2,053 lakhs carried forward as at 31st March 2025 and has made additional tax provisions of Rs 634 lakhs for earlier years.

Emphasis of Matter: Note No 40 - In reference to Note 30 of the standalone financial statements of the associate company, regarding the recognition of additional tariff revenue and carrying cost consequent to the judgement dated 3rd September 2025 of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL), which has granted the associate company an enforceable right to recover additional tariff and carrying cost from Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL). The APTEL has remanded the matter to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) for passing consequential orders. Pending such orders, the associate has recognised Rs 2,975 lakhs and Rs 1,548 lakhs as Exceptional Items pertaining to prior periods, and Rs 326 lakhs and Rs 34 lakhs as current year Revenue from Operations and Other Income respectively.

outlook.statement: FY 2026-27 shaping up as year of recovery and reset; industry forecasters converge on 6-7% CAGR for paper consumption; packaging/paperboard to remain dominant engine; printing/writing paper to gain traction from NEP 2020 and education spending; tissue/hygiene paper expected double-digit growth; specialty papers to see double-digit growth and higher realisations; margins expected to continue recovery from FY26; export business expected to be strong if US tariff levels remain; domestic market expected to grow with wide product offerings and flexibility in product mix; first half FY27 margins affected by cost push on imported inputs (pulp, waste paper, chemicals, coal) due to West Asia war crises; global supply chain volatility increasing input costs; international paper prices not recovering; cheaper imports from China/Indonesia continue; price increases announced but implementation depends on weakening import competition

India's macro-economic environment in FY 2025-26 is broadly supportive with real GDP growth of 6.6-7.4%, softening inflation, front-loaded capex, and benign interest rates. Packaging board demand expected to grow at 8-9% CAGR through FY2030 driven by e-commerce, food delivery, organised retail, FMCG expansion and plastic substitution mandates. Education sector demand from NEP 2020 provides floor for P&W segment. Tissue/hygiene growing at 7-8%. Company's strategic shift toward packaging and specialty papers is primary mitigation against P&W digitisation headwinds. Investment in solar/wind power under Group Captive model will reduce energy cost exposure and Scope 2 emissions. Wet ESP installation at Erode (first in Indian paper industry) to control particulate emissions.
outlook.period: FY 2025-26 and medium term through FY2030

outlook.statement: IPMA estimates domestic paper demand growing at 6-7% per annum, with packaging and tissue sub-segments growing at 8-10% per annum. India has the domestic capacity to be self-sufficient in most paper grades and has an opportunity to develop as a net exporter in select speciality grades.
Wind power to the Company's operations will significantly reduce Scope 2 GHG emissions and the Company's carbon footprint, aligning with India's national renewable energy targets.
Printing and writing paper segment expected to be negatively impacted in near future; company diversifying product range and strengthening marketing network and supply chain
Company has achieved Wood Positive Status and over 60% of energy needs in Unit Erode addressed through renewable energy sources/bio-fuels; further steps being taken to increase share

The Company continuously works on reduction in usage of fossil fuel, thro' increased use of bio-fuels. The following projects are under evaluation for reducing GHG: Exploring the possibilities to utilize available biomass within the system and use it as fuel. For Heat utilisation from coal fired boiler's flue gas to dry biomass, we are working with Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL). EESL has completed the bidding process for the LGWHR solution & all formalities are expected to be completed shortly. We are installing one more soot blower in the super heater zone in CPP to further step up usage of biomass. The Company, as a consumer shareholder, has recently entered into Share Purchase Agreement (SPA), Share Subscription & Shareholders' Agreement (SSSHA), Energy Supply Agreement and Performance Incentive Agreement with M/s.Navia One Power Private Limited (Solar & Wind Power generating SPV) and its Promoter shareholders, under Group Captive model, for the purpose of meeting the Solar Power & Wind Power requirements of the Company. The Solar and Wind power from the SPV is expected to be available by Q-1 of FY27.
Aiming to fully utilize the green power (Solar & Wind) for the plant operations.
Planning to establish pulpwood plantations in 1,500 acres through contract farming.
